subject: lion
pitch: A proud old lion resting with his head held high. A huge shaggy mane fading from golden blond at the face to dark chocolate at the edges, a tawny body with a pale cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, a broad black nose, a scar across one eyebrow, big padded paws and a long tail ending in a dark tuft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a sphinx-like resting lion pose for the rig, with front legs extended forward, hind legs folded, and tail extended out to the side, keeping the proportions manageable for a single TypeScript module.

I'm working out the skeleton structure: a root joint at the hips, a spine chain built with catmull points running up to the chest, then a neck chain leading to head and jaw joints, making sure chain parenting starts from the root joint since there's no existing joint to attach to otherwise. I'm also planning the body as a loft using the spine chain as its bone reference.

Now I'm placing body loft stations along the spine, adjusting their heights so the lion's belly touches the floor while the spine joints sit slightly higher, working out positions and widths from rump to chest.

Now I'm setting up the countershading paint and building the spine joint chain running from tail to shoulders, then a separate neck chain connecting up toward the mane, parenting it off the last spine joint so the whole skeleton flows together.

Next I'm sweeping a tapering tube along the neck path for shape, then placing the head joint and starting the skull geometry as a sphere positioned at the front of the neck.

Now I'm laying out the muzzle and jaw structure: a jaw joint for articulation, separate lower jaw box, upper muzzle box, a small black nose block, and amber eye spheres positioned symmetrically on the skull front.

Working out the eye placement so it sits partly embedded in the skull surface at the right depth, then positioning the brow box above it and figuring the scar's position and angle across the eyebrow so it lies flush against the curved skull surface rather than floating above it.

Now I'm sketching the ears as small spheres with darker inner coloring, then thinking through how to build the mane as layered shaggy clumps around the neck with a radial gradient running from golden near the face to dark brown at the outer edges, using a custom paint function to compute that color falloff.

I'm planning the mane geometry as a large faceted central mass behind the face, plus a surrounding ring of spike tufts to give it a shaggy, low-poly look.

For the tufts, I'll scatter small cone meshes across the mane surface flowing backward and down, keeping the count around 110 to balance detail against triangle budget and chart packing for the painted texture. I'll also add a lower belly fringe ellipsoid behind the chest to extend the mane's silhouette.

Varying tuft scale slightly for natural shagginess, and I want to avoid tufts pointing straight at the face near the mane's front edge — I should filter out hits too close to that region before sticking cones on.

I'll simplify the tuft filtering to just distance from the face center instead. For mane coloring I'm blending gold near the face through amber brown to dark at the edges using a three-stop gradient, and adding a second mane ellipsoid near the chest/shoulder for the belly fur, merging both into the tuft scatter. Now I'm moving on to the body's base paint with a tawny countershading scheme.

For the legs, I'm laying out the front limbs extended forward in a lying pose, chaining shoulder-elbow-wrist joints along a polyline path, parenting them to the spine.

Then I'm sweeping tapered leg geometry with shrinking radii toward the paws, adding ellipsoid paw shapes scaled flatter and longer, plus small toe-bump spheres on each paw for detail.

Now I'm working out the hind leg positions for a lying pose, placing haunch, hip, knee, and hock joints so the leg bends naturally and the foot extends forward along the ground.

I'll settle on 4 named points per leg (hip, knee, hock, paw) with 3 spans, using a polyline sweep so the joints stay sharp rather than overshooting like a smooth curve would. For the hind thigh mass, I'm placing a scaled, tawny-painted sphere at the hip bone position, and planning a similar sphere for the hind paw.

Working out the actual joint coordinates for the hind leg, I'm trying to mimic a lying lion's pose: knee pointing forward, shin angling back to the hock, then the paw flat on the ground slightly forward again. There's some overlap in the z-range between joints, but since it's all contained within the haunch mass, it should read fine visually even if the raw polyline technically crosses itself.

Now I'm checking that the hind paw position doesn't poke outside the body silhouette, so I'm nudging the x-coordinates for the hind points outward to match the body's half-width. Then I'm setting up the tail as a curling chain of joints running from the rump backward, defining the catmull-rom points, parenting it to the root, and tapering the radius toward a tuft at the tip.

For the tuft itself, I'm considering a stretched sphere aimed along the tail's tangent direction at the endpoint, then adding a ring of small cone spikes around it for a furry tip effect.

Still writing cone placement logic...

For the head details, I'm adding cream muzzle pads with whisker dots, a lower jaw box, small white canine cones, a tawny eyebrow ridge, and ear spheres tucked into the mane.

I'm setting up the jaw joint and head joint hierarchy, making sure each part binds to the right bone so mane tufts and head pieces deform together, then moving into the body loft construction.

For the body, I'm using the spine chain for the sweep so it deforms correctly, checking that the spine path stations and clamping handle the hind section without gaps. I'm adding countershading for the cream belly and muzzle based on surface normal, then starting on simple paw paint colors for the legs.

Now I'm defining the head colors—tawny fur, cream muzzle, dark nose, amber eyes with black pupils, and pale teeth—then placing the toe spheres on each paw with small offsets, checking that their radii line up so the paw bottoms sit flush with the ground along with the forearm and elbow geometry.

I'm positioning the shoulder mass but deciding to skip adding a separate sphere since the mane covers it, then building out the hind thigh and hind paw spheres with scaled radii to keep proportions and ground contact correct, and setting up the hind leg bone names (hip, knee, hock, paw) for each side.

Now I'm sweeping the hind leg taper from thigh through hock to paw, checking radii stay plausible at each joint, and deciding to skip extra details like scars, tufts, and whisker dots to keep things simple before moving into writing the actual code with left/right sign loops and the paint/mix color blending utility.

I'm defining a mane paint function that blends gold, brown, and dark tones based on distance from the face and adds a subtle noise-driven streak for texture, then reusing that same paint function for tufts so their tips naturally darken by position. Setting the tuft count to 130.

For the stick geometry, I'm using a shared open cone mesh with low radial segments, applying random per-tuft scaling for size variation, and orienting tufts outward across the surface to create a shaggy, hedgehog-like lion mane effect.

That handles the frame orientation fine, with face-near tufts sweeping backward into the mane naturally. Now I'm placing the ears—small scaled spheres positioned near the top of the head in tawny dark tones to match the bone coloring.

Adding brow ridge and scar details...
